transcript.speaker: Girish Pai, BOB Capital Markets
transcript.text: I wanted to ask about the TCV number, which is down quarter-on-quarter quite a bit both from large deal and the total TCV perspective. Were these numbers up to your expectations? If not, what exactly transpired in the quarter?

transcript.speaker: CEO
transcript.text: As far as our TCV of quarter two is concerned, we had few deals where the contract could not be signed on time, because of which they're slipping to this quarter. And both the deals that we could not sign will get signed. As far as we are concerned, the pipeline is very robust.

transcript.speaker: Girish Pai, BOB Capital Markets
transcript.text: Lastly, when is the salary increase going to happen?

transcript.speaker: CFO
transcript.text: Girish, you would note we just gave a salary increase effective 1st March 2025 -- sorry, 2026. So it's been just a few months since we rolled out. So right now, it's not under consideration.

transcript.speaker: Sudheer Guntupalli, Kotak Mahindra AMC
transcript.text: any thoughts on using your cash-rich balance sheet to make, you know, very big bang acquisitions like we had done in the cloud wave, be it the likes of Capco, Rizing , etc.?

transcript.speaker: CEO
transcript.text: As far as, acquisitions are concerned, our strategy will continue to be the same. We will look at opportunities that can enhance our value. Just to give you a context here, if you look at the acquisition that we made with Harman DTS, it actually gave us capabilities around design to manufacture and connected services.

transcript.speaker: Ravi Menon, Axis Capital
transcript.text: Is there anything that's holding us back, any client -specific issues, anything like that in BFSI? Or is consulting not really picking up, and these are more vendor consolidation deals that others have seen?

transcript.speaker: CEO
transcript.text: Additionally, if you remember, a specific customer in BFSI Europe had earlier decided to move part of the work to their captive, which impacted our revenue. The good news is that we are now seeing good momentum building up with this customer, and it is reflecting in the growth numbers in the current quarter and going forward.

transcript.speaker: Sandeep Shah, Equirus Securities
transcript.text: And just the last question, you also said that going forward margins may keep increasing despite investment. So do you believe we may again by Q4 be in the target range of 17, 17.5?

transcript.speaker: CFO
transcript.text: So yes, I do think that you know, from a we would like to get back to the band as quickly as possible, but we're not putting a timeline out there.

transcript.speaker: Girish Pai, BOB Capital Markets
transcript.text: And the question on deflation, where are we in the cycle?

transcript.speaker: CFO
transcript.text: Typically, our contracts are about 2 to 2.5 years in terms of the average tenor, right? And we've been in this cycle for at least last 2 years and or thereabouts, 1.5 to 2 years. So in some sense, a lot of the contracts that we've had have been refreshed and renewed. So in some sense that we should be at that inflection curve in a few quarters.

transcript.speaker: Vibhor Singhal, Nuvama Equities
transcript.text: Healthcare is a vertical where I think a lot of companies in our space are very excited about, and they're opening up their new basically verticals in terms of healthcare, which suggests to suggesting to us that there is very little outsourcing penetration in this segment. So how do -- what does our takeaway in this sector, reasons for our slightly low, I understand, lower growth or decline in this quarter, and how do you see the vertical going over the next few quarters?

transcript.speaker: CEO
transcript.text: As far as health as a sector, especially in the US, it is impacted by policy changes, and large US payers despite this, very intensely focused on cost takeout and also operational efficiencies, because the membership growth is slowing down, and their margins are remaining continues to remain under pressure.

transcript.speaker: Ashwin Mehta, Ambit Capital
transcript.text: So you've seen health exchange enrollments drop by almost 18% in June. We typically used to do this business, so just want to get a sense on how big is this business in our healthcare vertical, and how do you see this playing out in the December quarter, because typically that's where the peak enrollment season kicks in?

transcript.speaker: CEO
transcript.text: As far as we are concerned, we don't call out that specific number, Ashwin. We just give the overall health numbers. And like I said, that we had we did have an impact because of some of the policy-related changes that happened to some of the payer US payers.

transcript.speaker: Ashwin Mehta, Ambit Capital
transcript.text: in terms of the head count cuts this quarter, what was the driver for that?

transcript.speaker: Saurabh Govil, CHRO
transcript.text: From the headcount, if you look at it, year -on-year it's flattish. So and particularly in this year this quarter, if you look at it, first half, we didn't go on campus. So, that's the thing. We will be going to campuses to hire given the volume growth in the second half. So I think it'll even out as we move forward. We're also driving productivity from AI projects.

transcript.speaker: Dipesh Mehta, Emkay Global
transcript.text: Second question is about the two deal which you referred, which got delayed in terms of signing. Whether we close both the deal in terms of signing this quarter or it is yet to be signed kind of thing?

transcript.speaker: CFO
transcript.text: Like Srini said, they are in the process of being signed, and we're confident of securing both the deals, and we will share that with you when we meet next in January.

transcript.speaker: Gaurav Rateria, Morgan Stanley
transcript.text: Is there also an element of the deals getting pushed out, which kind of haven't has an impact on the guidance in 3Q, and if the deal wins get bunched up in 3Q, could that have a positive influence on the 4Q revenue conversion metrics?

transcript.speaker: CFO
transcript.text: Yes, Gaurav. The short answer to that is yes, it will have a positive impact on the quarter four outlook for revenue. To your other point on whether the quarter three guidance includes the impact of some of these large deals getting pushed. You know, we guide in a range, right? Obviously, the and what you should look at the guidance factoring and the majority, I mean, what is really largely leaving this is basically the furloughs and lower working days.

Constant currency (CC) for a period is the product of volumes in that period times the average actual exchange rate of the corresponding comparative period.

Total Bookings refers to the total contract value of all orders that were booked during the period including new orders, renewals, and increases to existing contracts. Bookings do not reflect subsequent terminations or reductions related to bookings originally recorded in prior fiscal periods.
Large deal bookings consist of deals greater than or equal to $30 million in total contract value.
IT Services Operating Margin refers to Segment Results Total as reflected in IFRS financial.

remarks:
Srini Pallia, CEO and Managing Director, said, “The strategic investments we have been making are beginning to deliver results. They are enhancing our ability to win in new markets, add new clients, and grow existing relationships. At the same time, our consulting -led, AI-powered strategy is helping us create larger transformation opportunities. W e see AI as a long-term growth driver that will expand the addressable market for technology and business transformation. We are already seeing its potential reflected in the momentum across our AI-Native Unit and AI offerings portfolio”.

Aparna Iyer, Chief Financial Officer, said, “Our operating margin for the quarter was 16.5%, an expansion of 0.5% sequentially. We have delivered this improvement even while continuing to invest in our business and people. We remain relentless in driving cash flow conversion. Q2 is yet another quarter where our operating cash flow has been robust and stood at 166% of net income.”

provenance.caveats: IFRS, not Ind AS. Reports operating margin (16.5%), not EBITDA. Segments (IT Services by SMU/sector) and Q3 revenue guidance ($2,571-2,625M) present. Operating cash flow 165.8% of net income. Transcript is the Q2 FY27 call of 15 Oct 2026 (same quarter).
